newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Everbright-IHD on track for finance sector.
newsitem.headline: Everbright-IHD on track for finance sector.

text.p: China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd took a major step forward on Friday in its strategy to become a financial services conglomerate by winning approval to take a stake in a mainland Chinese bank.

Everbright-IHD said Chinese authorities had approved the acquisition by its controlling shareholder, China Everbright Holdings Ltd, of a 20 percent stake in Everbright Bank of China from Beijing-based China Everbright Group Ltd.
Everbright Holdings plans to then transfer the stake to Everbright-IHD, it said.
"The company intends to begin a process of due diligence on Everbright Bank of China and negotiations with the controlling shareholder immediately," Everbright-IHD said.

Everbright-IHD was seen making a bid to become a financial conglomerate since it bought a 20 percent stake in International Bank of Asia Ltd and a five percent stake in insurer National Mutual Asia Ltd from its parent.

Earlier this month, the company said it had raised HK$1.88 billion before expenses through a new share placement, of which HK$380 million would go to reduce debt with the balance earmarked to acquire a stake in Everbright Bank.

Analysts estimated that the cost of the acquisition would range between HK$1.2 billion and HK$1.6 billion based on the bank's 1996 earnings of 891 million yuan. As at end 1995, Everbright Bank had total assets of 52.9 billion yuan.
Everbright Bank is one of China's few commercial banks. It was restructured into a joint stock company in January with the issue of 1.37 billion new shares to 131 other shareholders.
The Asian Development Bank took a three percent stake, and Everbright Group's stake fell to 51 percent from 100 percent.

Everbright Group itself is a major Chinese enterprise under the control of China's State Council. Its chairman is Zhu Xiaohua, a former deputy head of China's central bank, who is also chairman of Everbright Holdings and Everbright-IHD.
Zhu told an investment seminar in Hong Kong last week that there would be greater cooperation between Everbright Bank and International Bank of Asia (IBA).
"We also want to provide some advantages to IBA in China but so far we have done anything as yet," the chairman said.
"I believe the banking sector in China has a bright future because of the high (economic) growth rate," he added.
Zhu said Everbright Bank had upgraded and modernised its risk management and internal auditing systems with the help of the Asian Development Bank.
"These changes will help the bank's performance," he said. "We follow the market rather than policy, but we also consider government policy as well as profitability."
The chairman also stressed the bank's nationwide links, the growing competition in Shanghai, and the bank's intention to explore new areas.
"The market situation has already changed," said Zhu. "Now We want to explore the hinterland. We are going to open a branch in Kunming then a branch in Wuhan."
The bank, which is headquartered in Beijing, has branches in Shanghai, Heilongjiang, Changchun, Qingdao, Yantai, Dalian, Chongqing, Shenzhen and Haikou.
